$comment: JSON has no comment syntax, so every entry carries a `sources` object -- one citation string per numeric field. That is the 'comment next to each entry' the brief asks for, in the only form this file format allows.

EMBODIED CARBON: the published factors are per kilogram (kgCO2e/kg, cradle-to-gate A1-A3). embodiedCarbon_kgCO2e_m3 is therefore density x factor, and each `sources.embodiedCarbon` string shows that arithmetic so it can be rechecked.

Primary carbon source: IStructE, 'A brief guide to calculating embodied carbon', The Structural Engineer, July 2020, Table 2 'A1A3 ECFs for typical structural materials' (values drawn from ICE V3 and product EPDs).

COST is the weakest data here: it is regional, volatile and rarely published per cubic metre. Every cost carries costConfidence 'indicative' and is order-of-magnitude only. TODO: replace with RSMeans or a regional cost database before any number is presented as authoritative.

sources.density: EN 1991-1-1 Table A.1: reinforced concrete 25 kN/m^3 -> 2400 kg/m^3 (normal-weight concrete 2300 + ~100 for reinforcement).
sources.yieldStrength: Characteristic cylinder compressive strength f'c = 30 MPa (C30/37, EN 206). Concrete has no yield point; this is the governing compressive strength.
sources.embodiedCarbon: IStructE TSE Jul-2020 Table 2 (ICE V3): unreinforced C32/40 @25% GGBS = 0.120 kgCO2e/kg; reinforcement bar, worldsteel world average = 1.99 kgCO2e/kg. Assuming 120 kg rebar/m^3: 2280 kg x 0.120 + 120 kg x 1.99 = 273.6 + 238.8 = 512.4 -> 512 kgCO2e/m^3.
sources.cost: INDICATIVE. US supply-and-place ready-mix incl. reinforcement and formwork, order ~700 USD/m^3. TODO: replace with RSMeans.

sources.youngsModulus: EN 1993-1-1 §3.2.6: E = 210 GPa; ASTM A992 / AISC 360 use 200 GPa (29,000 ksi). 200 GPa adopted.
sources.yieldStrength: EN 10025-2 S355, nominal yield strength 355 MPa for t <= 16 mm.
sources.embodiedCarbon: IStructE TSE Jul-2020 Table 2 (ICE V3): structural sections, worldsteel world average = 1.55 kgCO2e/kg. 7850 x 1.55 = 12,167.5 -> 12,168 kgCO2e/m^3. NOTE: UK British Steel EPD is 2.45 and European Bauforumstahl 1.13 -- a >2x spread. The world average is used as the region-neutral default.
sources.cost: INDICATIVE. Statista Canada 2025: universal beams ~4500 CAD/tonne ~= 3300 USD/tonne; x 7.85 t/m^3 ~= 26,000 USD/m^3 material only, excludes fabrication and erection. TODO: replace.

sources.density: Spruce CLT, typical mean density 470-500 kg/m^3 (EN 338 C24 lamellae, rho_mean 420 kg/m^3, plus adhesive and densification). 480 adopted.
sources.youngsModulus: EN 338 C24 E0,mean = 11.0 GPa for the lamellae. Measured whole-panel values are lower (8.0-10.2 GPa reported in CLT bending studies) because of the cross layers; 11.0 GPa is the major-strength-direction lamella value. TODO: switch to an effective panel EI if panel layup becomes a design variable.
sources.yieldStrength: EN 338 C24 characteristic bending strength fm,k = 24 MPa. Timber does not yield; this is the characteristic bending strength.
sources.embodiedCarbon: IStructE TSE Jul-2020 Table 2 (ICE V3): CLT, 100% FSC/PEFC = 0.437 kgCO2e/kg, EXCLUDING sequestration. 480 x 0.437 = 209.8 -> 210 kgCO2e/m^3. Including biogenic sequestration this figure would go negative; excluding it is the conservative convention and matches the cited table.
sources.cost: INDICATIVE. Supplied CLT panel, order ~1400 USD/m^3. TODO: replace.

sources.density: EN 14080 Table 5, GL24h: rho_k = 385 kg/m^3 (characteristic). Mean density rho_mean ~= 420 kg/m^3 is used here, since self-weight should use mean not characteristic values.
sources.yieldStrength: EN 14080 GL24h: characteristic bending strength fm,g,k = 24 MPa (the '24' in the grade designation).
sources.embodiedCarbon: IStructE TSE Jul-2020 Table 2 (ICE V3): glulam, 100% FSC/PEFC = 0.512 kgCO2e/kg, excluding sequestration. 420 x 0.512 = 215.0 -> 215 kgCO2e/m^3.
sources.cost: INDICATIVE. Reported glulam ranges span 100-2000 USD/m^3 depending on grade and section; ~1800 USD/m^3 taken for structural-grade sections. TODO: replace.

sources.density: Laminated bamboo lumber measured at 635 kg/m^3; review values span 600-700 kg/m^3 (Sharma et al., 'Development of Laminated Bamboo Lumber: Review', UMass; J. Wood Sci. 2023 ISO 23478 testing). 650 adopted.
sources.youngsModulus: Laminated bamboo lumber, modulus of elasticity 9,643 MPa = 9.6 GPa in compression parallel to grain (J. Wood Sci. 2023, ISO 23478-2022 testing of N-finity LBL). Review range 8.7-12 GPa.
sources.yieldStrength: Compressive strength parallel to grain 58.7 MPa (same source). Review range 34-84 MPa, so this is mid-range, not a characteristic design value. TODO: replace with a characteristic (5th-percentile) value once a design standard is adopted -- ISO 23478 is recent and national design values are still emerging.
sources.embodiedCarbon: Cradle-to-gate LCA of laminated bamboo and bamboo-timber composites reports 210.3, 314.2, 322.3 and 473.3 kgCO2e/m^3 across specimen types (MDPI Sustainability, 'Cold-Press Manufacturing of Laminated Bamboo and Bamboo-Timber Composites: A Life-Cycle Carbon Assessment'). 322 adopted as the mid-range specimen value, excluding the ~1140 kgCO2e/m^3 of biogenic storage reported elsewhere, for consistency with the timber entries.
sources.cost: INDICATIVE and weakly grounded -- laminated structural bamboo has no established per-m^3 market price outside Asia. ~1200 USD/m^3 assumed. TODO: replace, and treat comparisons against this entry with caution.

sources.density: Cement-stabilised rammed earth (CSRE) tested at dry densities of 15.7-19.62 kN/m^3 -> 1600-2000 kg/m^3 (Venkatarama Reddy et al., CSRE compressive strength studies). 2000 kg/m^3 adopted for a well-compacted mix.
sources.youngsModulus: APPROXIMATE -- TODO verify. CSRE modulus rises 2.5-5x across the 15.7-19.62 kN/m^3 density range and 1-3x as cement content goes 5% -> 12% (Reddy & Kumar, 'Cement stabilised rammed earth Part B: compressive strength and stress-strain characteristics'). Reported moduli cluster in the 500-3000 MPa band; 1.0 GPa taken as a mid estimate. This is the least certain stiffness in the library.
sources.yieldStrength: Unconfined compressive strength of CSRE typically 2-5 MPa for practical cement contents (Reddy et al.; ASCE JMCE 'Structural Behavior of Story-High Cement-Stabilized Rammed-Earth Walls under Compression'). 3.0 MPa adopted. Highly stabilised laboratory mixes reach 9.3 MPa but are not representative.
sources.embodiedCarbon: 177.73 kgCO2e/m^3 reported for an optimised stabilised rammed earth mixture (Sci. Rep. 2025, 'Thermal insulation and mechanical performance of sustainable rammed earth walls incorporating construction and demolition waste and calcium oxide', s41598-025-30472-w) -> 178. NOTE: this is for one specific stabilised mix; unstabilised rammed earth is far lower, and cement content dominates the result. Cross-check: Reddy & Kumar (Energy & Buildings 2010) give 400-500 MJ/m^3 embodied energy for 6-8% cement CSRE, consistent with a low-hundreds kgCO2e/m^3 figure.
sources.cost: INDICATIVE. Labour-intensive but material-cheap; ~450 USD/m^3 assumed. TODO: replace.

sources.density: EN 1991-1-1 Table A.1: masonry of fired clay units, 18-20 kN/m^3 -> 1900 kg/m^3 for the assembly including mortar.
sources.youngsModulus: TMS 402/ACI 530 §4.2.2: Em = 700 * f'm for clay masonry = 700 * 10 = 7000 MPa = 7.0 GPa.
sources.yieldStrength: Characteristic masonry compressive strength f'm = 10 MPa, a common design value for solid fired clay units in Type S mortar. Masonry does not yield; this is a compressive strength.
sources.embodiedCarbon: IStructE TSE Jul-2020 Table 2 (ICE V3): single engineering clay brick, generic UK = 0.213 kgCO2e/kg. 1900 x 0.213 = 404.7 -> 405 kgCO2e/m^3. NOTE: the 0.213 factor is for the brick alone; applying it to the full assembly density slightly overstates the mortar's contribution and understates nothing, so it errs high.
sources.cost: INDICATIVE. Supply-and-lay loadbearing brickwork, order ~900 USD/m^3. TODO: replace.

sources.density: Aluminium Association / ASM: 6061 alloy density 2700 kg/m^3.
sources.youngsModulus: Aluminum Design Manual (AA ADM) Table A.3.1 / ASM: E = 68.9 GPa (10,000 ksi) for 6xxx series.
sources.yieldStrength: ASTM B221 6061-T6: minimum tensile yield strength 276 MPa (40 ksi).
sources.embodiedCarbon: ICE database, European average extruded aluminium profiles = 6.83 kgCO2e/kg. 2700 x 6.83 = 18,441 kgCO2e/m^3. NOTE: this figure is extremely sensitive to recycled content and grid mix -- primary virgin aluminium is ~13.1 kgCO2e/kg and 100% secondary ~0.5 kgCO2e/kg, a 26x spread. The European average is the region-neutral default and is deliberately unflattering to aluminium, which is the honest teaching outcome.
sources.cost: INDICATIVE. Extruded structural aluminium, order ~12,000 USD/m^3. TODO: replace.
